summary: Targeted 5 load-bearing brief claims for counter-evidence: (1) the single-source '30% user increase' from Hallow parish partnerships, (2) the triple-cited-but-single-event Lent/Easter calendar-timing growth figures (412%/230%), (3) the 'authenticity beats slick production' faith-audience claim, which sits in unexamined tension with the brief's own Hallow celebrity-ad growth story, (4) Adapty's vendor-sourced referral LTV/trust statistics used to justify prioritizing referral over paid acquisition, and (5) the core self-flagged extrapolation that Hallow's/YouVersion's scale-dependent tactics transfer to FellowScript's smaller, group/study-centric, non-devotional niche. All five are load-bearing for the brief's top recommendations and currently rest on thinner or less-independent sourcing than their confident phrasing implies.
